llm.summary: The skill purports to provide P2P Agent communication and automated VPS deployment, and it contains deployment scripts and remote‑SSH actions, but the bundle also includes many unrelated components and hardcoded sensitive values which do not align cleanly with its declared metadata—review before use.

dimensions.detail: The README/SKILL.md describes Portal/Bridge deployment and needs SSH/API keys (reasonable), but the package contains large unrelated projects (weibo plugin, stock-analysis, self-improving-agent, many other skills) and many files from a development workspace. Registry metadata initially reported no required envs, while SKILL.md includes multiple required env vars. The presence of many unrelated modules and workspace files is disproportionate to a single 'Agent P2P' skill and suggests a sloppy or accidental bundle of a full developer workspace.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and AGENTS.md direct the agent to read local configuration and memory files (e.g., ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, ~/.openclaw/gateway.env, MEMORY.md, AGENTS.md), to run local scripts (send.py, send_file.py, auto_install.py), and to perform SSH actions to remote VPSes. AGENTS.md even instructs 'Don't ask permission. Just do it.'—this expands scope beyond narrowly deploying/using a Portal and instructs reading of potentially sensitive local state and acting autonomously.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No formal registry install spec, but multiple included scripts (auto_install.py, deploy_portal.py, setup.sh, deploy_agent_p2p.sh) will install packages, write config files, SSH to remote servers, run certbot, configure systemd, and start services. Auto-install actions involve remote execution and writing sensitive files (~/.openclaw/gateway.env, /etc/nginx/.htpasswd). The implicit install/run behavior is high-impact and not limited to local, transient operations.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md requests AGENTP2P_API_KEY, AGENTP2P_HUB_URL, OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL, OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN—these are plausible for the feature set. However the package contains hardcoded secrets and environment tokens (e.g., an Authorization Bearer token in TOOLS.md, API keys and VPS credentials found in MEMORY.md), and the agent is instructed to read other files for tokens. The number and sensitivity of credentials and the inclusion of unrelated hardcoded tokens are disproportionate and risky.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (not force-included) and model invocation allowed (normal). Nonetheless the skill's scripts write persistent configuration (~/.openclaw/gateway.env and ~/.openclaw/agent-p2p-admin.txt), create systemd services on a VPS, and store credentials on disk. While persistence actions are coherent with deploying a long-running Portal, combined with the other concerns (reading local memory, hardcoded secrets, broad workspace contents) this increases potential blast radius.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package contains real deployment scripts that will: read local OpenClaw configuration, write ~/.openclaw/gateway.env, use SSH to log into your VPS and run apt/certbot/git/etc., and create services on the remote host. Additionally, the bundle includes many unrelated projects and some hardcoded secrets (API tokens, VPS IP, SSH key paths, admin passwords) in files like MEMORY.md and TOOLS.md. Before installing or running anything: 1) don't provide high‑privilege secrets (owner API keys, your main SSH private key) — use a dedicated, limited SSH key and limited Hooks token; 2) inspect the repository locally (search for any hardcoded tokens, IPs, or passwords) and remove sensitive developer data; 3) run installation in an isolated VM/container or on a throwaway account/VPS to test; 4) if you intend to deploy to your VPS, review auto_install.py and remote scripts line-by-line (they will run sudo, apt, certbot, and write files remotely); 5) verify the upstream source (the SKILL.md claims a GitHub repo — confirm it and prefer a clean GitHub clone rather than publishing your local workspace); 6) if you are not comfortable auditing code, do not run auto_install.py or the deploy scripts and prefer manual guided setup. Given the mixed/accidental workspace content and embedded secrets, treat this skill as untrusted until cleaned and source-verified.
llm.findings: [base64-block] unexpected: A base64-block prompt-injection pattern was detected in SKILL.md; this can indicate embedded obfuscated content or an attempt to influence evaluation/runtime instructions. No benign reason apparent from the documentation to include such blocks.
